headline: Lambda, a cloud company that rents out AI computing power, is raising up to $4 billion at a $14.5 billion valuation before a planned 2027 stock-market listing, the Wall Street Journal reports.
score_reason: Facts match the headline; the story is a WSJ exclusive read through TechCrunch.
importance_line: Investors are still funding suppliers of AI computing, which matters to the lenders and customers involved, but the valuation may lean heavily on one customer, Anthropic.
summary: The Wall Street Journal reports, as relayed by TechCrunch, that Lambda, a so-called neocloud (a company that rents out AI computing power), is raising up to $4 billion at a valuation of $14.5 billion before the new money is added, in what could be its last private round before a planned 2027 IPO; Coatue Management and Blackstone are leading it. A letter to investors seen by the Journal shows its order backlog grew from $15 billion in June to $50 billion in September, with much of the rise apparently from a $35 billion commitment by Anthropic, so TechCrunch notes the valuation may depend heavily on Anthropic's ability to keep paying.
notes: WSJ paywalled; read TechCrunch's account of the WSJ exclusive. The TechCrunch comment on Anthropic dependence is TechCrunch's analysis, labelled as such in the summary.
